clue.text: You can get such things beneath the vendor's place of business being so bodied.

parts.note: beneath means under
a vendor sells from a stall or stand
able-bodied: the word that fits 'so' in 'so bodied' is able

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about goods stored under a market stall, with a stray comment on physique.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'things you can get', i.e. grasp mentally. 'Being so bodied' asks which word goes before -bodied: able.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to grasp it mentally, so things you can get are comprehensible.

clue.text: Not down where the guns might be kept, but one possibly knocks the stuffing out of things when one does.

definitions.text: one possibly knocks the stuffing out of things when one does

parts.note: the opposite of down is up

parts.words: where the guns might be kept
parts.note: holsters are the cases in which pistols are carried

explanation.surface: Someone keeps their guns raised rather than holstered, then does something violent to furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: someone who re-covers chairs may well strip the old stuffing out first.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who upholsters reworks padded furniture, often removing the old padding before restuffing it.

clue.text: Take away the value of improper trade, which should go to court shortly.

indicators.note: improper trade is trade done wrongly, so the letters of trade are put in a wrong order

parts.note: CT is the short form of court, as in street addresses

explanation.surface: Profits from crooked dealing should be confiscated and the case brought before a judge soon.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to lessen its worth, so taking away value is the same idea.

clue.text: If you make one it should at least stand for something!

definitions.text: If you make one it should at least stand for something!

parts.words: If you make one it should at least stand for something!
parts.note: making a formal protest or case to someone is 'making' one of these, and the word also means a thing that stands for, or symbolises, another

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand for' plays on two senses: to take a principled stand, and to symbolise. Making one of these to authorities means stating a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or symbol is something that stands for something else; a formal complaint is also made as one.

clue.text: Earthy land in France–one quarter English.

parts.note: terre is the French word for land
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A description of a rustic plot in France, a quarter of it owned by an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare adjective means of the earth or worldly, so it is a synonym for earthy.

clue.text: Argue over petty things to keep your spirits up over your broken leg.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for spirits is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: gin is a spirit

indicators.note: a broken leg is a damaged one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to someone laid up with a fracture: stay cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep your spirits up' looks like encouragement, but 'up' reads GIN upwards as NIG, and 'broken' turns LEG into GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To quibble or find fault over minor details is to bicker about trifles.

clue.text: See 1
It must contain chocolate to have something like cheese around it.

indicators.note: around tells us the cheese word goes about the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: A recipe rule: the dish needs chocolate and a cheesy coating.
explanation.definitionFit: This square cake is a chocolate bake by definition, so containing chocolate is its defining trait.

clue.text: Certainly not a rough tune for the late service.

parts.note: something certainly not rough is smooth or level, i.e. even
a tune is a song

explanation.surface: A choir's tune for the evening service is anything but rough.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Anglican service of evening prayer, held late in the day.

clue.text: Represented by the capital quality of Taurus–or just a rather stubborn quality?

definitions.text: Represented by the capital quality of Taurus
definitions.meaning: first meaning: Taurus is the bull, and its head (capital, from Latin caput) gives the quality of being bull-headed

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' here means of the head: the sign Taurus is drawn as a bull's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bullheaded means being obstinate, so the noun names a stubborn character trait.

clue.text: Shakespearean fellow, sort of shot up, right?

indicators.note: sort of means a version of, so the letters of shot up are re-sorted

explanation.surface: Asks whether a character in Shakespeare was more or less shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges SHOT UP into HOTSPU. Henry Percy, nicknamed Hotspur, is the fiery rebel in Henry IV Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Percy appears under this nickname as a character in Shakespeare's history play Henry IV Part 1.

clue.text: Clues go badly wrong: "It's a monosaccharide!"

indicators.note: things gone badly wrong are disordered, so the letters of clues go are scrambled

explanation.surface: A solver's clues have misfired, and a chemist blurts out a sugar's class.
explanation.definitionFit: Dextrose is a simple sugar of one ring, which is what a monosaccharide is.

clue.text: You won't drink the water if you do, and play it safe.

definitions.text: You won't drink the water if you do
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read literally: leave the well alone and you draw no water from it
second meaning: avoid meddling with something that is already fine

explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits the phrase into its literal words: leaving a well untouched means drinking none of its water.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means do not interfere with something that is satisfactory, a cautious course.

clue.text: Go over the limit, strangers (strangely enough) needing direction.

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters of strangers are put in an odd order

parts.note: S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Visitors from elsewhere need directions, perhaps after crossing a border.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to overstep a boundary, moral or legal, so it means exceed the limit.

clue.text: All tied up with an overseas New Year's celebration at this place, to start devotions.

parts.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival
here means at this place

indicators.note: to start points to the opening letter of the word devotions

parts.note: D is the first letter of devotions

explanation.surface: A busy person is booked up with a foreign New Year festival before religious observances begin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tet is the lunar New Year festival of Vietnam; 'to start' takes just the opening letter of devotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tethered is fastened with a rope, so it is literally tied up.

clue.text: Even disturbed by a word of hesitation, this would be a display only on the surface.

definitions.text: this would be a display only on the surface

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown out of order, so the letters of even are shifted

parts.note: er is the sound a hesitating speaker makes

explanation.surface: Even a nervous 'er' can spoil a polished front.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin attractive layer or a superficial show of a quality, hiding what lies beneath.

clue.text: They might be jabs to the jaw, but the civil type are of some concern.

definitions.text: They might be jabs to the jaw
definitions.meaning: first meaning: punches thrown with the right hand

definitions.text: the civil type are of some concern

explanation.walkthrough: A boxer's punches and a citizen's entitlements share this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers throw punches with either hand, and lawful entitlements share the same plural noun.

clue.text: Is the king upset about her being in such a pickle?

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other word
upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of king are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch is troubled about a woman who has landed him in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants 'pickle' to mean a predicament and 'upset' to describe the king's mood; instead 'upset' scrambles his title to GKIN, 'about' wraps it round the woman, and the pickle is a vinegar-preserved cucumber.
explanation.definitionFit: This small cucumber is almost always eaten preserved in vinegar, so it is a pickle.

clue.text: Swap evil-doing for this, but it's what one often does when seeking a new form of transportation.

definitions.text: it's what one often does when seeking a new form of transportation

parts.note: to swap is to trade
sin is wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Giving up wickedness for something better, like replacing an old car.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (6,2) splits the letters of 'trade sin' differently, into the phrase used when buying a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer of a new car typically hands the old one over as part payment, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: One might get such at the sauna, but it's a funny way to manipulate a feather!

definitions.text: One might get such at the sauna

parts.note: to manipulate muscles is to rub them, as a masseur does
down is soft fine feathering

explanation.surface: A spa massage likened to stroking a feather.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads 'rub down', a whimsical way of handling a feather, since down is a kind of feather.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage or brisk towelling given after a bath or exercise, a typical spa treatment.

clue.text: They often get a response, but you could find it mulish, almost.

indicators.note: you could find these letters in a new order, so the pieces are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: almost means all but the last letter of mulish is used

explanation.surface: Someone reacts badly to provocation and you call it stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the H from MULISH to leave MULIS; 'you could find' signals that IT plus those letters can be rearranged into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stimuli are things that provoke a reaction, so they often draw a response.

clue.text: Where one might expect to find a ringer, with a little spirit right by, surrounding it.

definitions.text: Where one might expect to find a ringer

indicators.note: surrounding means the word by encloses the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
an elf is a small sprite

explanation.surface: A spook seen beside a bell-ringer, perhaps in a church tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell tower is where bell-ringers work, so it is where a ringer would be found.

clue.text: A questionable labor practice, but a noteworthy achievement to the woman's place of rest at the sound of a bell.

parts.note: a feat is a notable accomplishment
her means belonging to a woman
a bed is where one rests

parts.words: at the sound of a bell
parts.note: ding is the noise a bell makes

explanation.surface: A feat of getting a woman to bed when a bell rings, alongside a dubious work rule.
explanation.definitionFit: This union practice requires hiring more workers than needed, which critics deem wasteful.

clue.text: Love–or so disturbed you think it's god?

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of the flower word are rearranged

parts.note: something roughly meaning love: the red rose is the traditional emblem of love, and 'or so' marks the match as approximate

explanation.surface: A lover so shaken that they mistake their beloved for a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or so' loosens 'Love' to its emblem, ROSE; 'disturbed' rearranges it. The question mark flags that this is the god of love himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek deity of desire, counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: What one may do to the lawn doesn't go on, but spoils the result.

parts.words: What one may do to the lawn
parts.note: one rakes a lawn to clear leaves and moss
a thing that doesn't go on is off

explanation.surface: Raking the lawn halts, and the result is ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoils' looks like a verb but is the noun: the plunder, and a rake-off is a share of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-off is an illicit cut of the proceeds, so it is loot taken from the outcome.

clue.text: Work with something too much and you'll get nothing on an important day with such a stratagem.

parts.note: O is a zero, nothing
VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945
a ruse is a trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: A warning that overwork earns you nothing on a big occasion if you scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day is 8 May 1945, Victory in Europe day.
explanation.definitionFit: To overuse something is to employ it excessively, working it beyond reasonable limits.

clue.text: See 8
My casting's not good, but you might be fit to indulge in them.

definitions.text: you might be fit to indulge in them

indicators.note: a casting that is not good needs redoing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor admits their role was miscast, unless physical fitness is required.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaulting and floor exercises demand athleticism, so a fit person can take part in them.
